questions.question: As a small finance bank, what must we include in our hiring process to screen staff who will handle KYC, AML, and CFT responsibilities?
questions.answer: We must establish an adequate screening mechanism, including a Know Your Employee/Staff policy, as an integral part of the personnel recruitment and hiring process.
questions.evidence: The bank shall put in place an adequate screening mechanism, including Know Your Employee / Staff policy, as an integral part of its personnel recruitment / hiring process.

questions.question: As a small finance bank, what should our ongoing KYC/AML/CFT staff training cover, and how should the training focus vary by staff role?
questions.answer: The bank must run an ongoing programme that adequately trains staff in KYC/AML/CFT policy, with different training focus for frontline staff, compliance staff, and staff dealing with new customers.
questions.evidence: The bank shall put in place an on-going employee training programme so that the members of staff are adequately trained in KYC / AML / CFT policy. The focus of the training shall be different for frontline staff, compliance staff and staff dealing with new customers.

unanswerable.question: What minimum number of KYC/AML/CFT training hours per employee per year must a small finance bank provide?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires an ongoing employee training programme with role-specific training focus, but it does not specify any minimum training hours, annual frequency, or completion deadline.

questions.question: When a payments bank opens a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG), must it complete customer due diligence (CDD) for every member of the SHG?
questions.answer: No. A payments bank need not complete CDD for every SHG member when opening the group’s savings bank account.
questions.evidence: (1) The bank shall not require CDD of all the members of an SHG while opening the savings bank account of the SHG.

questions.question: When a payments bank opens a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG), whose CDD is sufficient?
questions.answer: CDD of all the SHG’s office bearers is sufficient.
questions.evidence: (2) The CDD of all the office bearers shall suffice.

unanswerable.question: Is there a deadline for a payments bank to complete CDD of all office bearers after opening a savings bank account for a Self Help Group (SHG)?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies whose CDD is required but does not state any deadline for completing it.

questions.question: As a payments bank, if we delay reporting a transaction to the Director, FIU-IND, how is each day of delay counted when assessing violations?
questions.answer: Each day of delay beyond the time limit specified in the Rule is treated as a separate violation, so the delay is counted day by day rather than as one breach.
questions.evidence: a delay of each day in not reporting a transaction or delay of each day in rectifying a mis-represented transaction beyond the time limit as specified in the Rule shall constitute as a separate violation

questions.question: As a payments bank, may we restrict operations in a customer's account simply because we have filed a suspicious transaction report with the FIU-IND?
questions.answer: No. The bank is not permitted to place any restriction on operations in the accounts merely on the basis of the STR filed.
questions.evidence: The bank shall not put any restriction on operations in the accounts merely on the basis of the STR filed.

unanswerable.question: As a payments bank, what is the exact number of days within which we must report a transaction or rectify a mis-reported transaction to the FIU-IND Director?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only says that each day of delay beyond the time limit specified in the Rule is a separate violation; it does not state the actual reporting or rectification deadline or the number of days allowed.

questions.question: What must a payments bank, its directors, officers, and employees keep confidential regarding PML records and information furnished to the Financial Intelligence Unit–India Director?
questions.answer: They must keep confidential both the fact that records required under rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005 are maintained and the fact that information is furnished to the Director.
questions.evidence: The bank, its directors, officers, and all employees shall ensure that the fact of maintenance of records referred to in rule 3 of the PML (Maintenance of Records) Rules, 2005, and furnishing of the information to the Director is confidential.

questions.question: Can a payments bank share information about an analysis of unusual transactions or activities despite its confidentiality obligations concerning PML records and FIU-India reporting?
questions.answer: Yes. The confidentiality requirement does not prevent sharing under paragraph 8 of the RBI’s Payments Banks KYC Directions, provided the bank has already conducted the analysis of transactions or activities that appear unusual.
questions.evidence: However, such confidentiality requirement shall not inhibit sharing of information under paragraph 8 of these Directions of any analysis of transactions and activities which appear unusual, if the bank has done any such analysis.

unanswerable.question: For how many years must a payments bank retain the PML records covered by the confidentiality requirement?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph imposes confidentiality obligations concerning record maintenance and furnishing information to the Director, but it does not state any record-retention period.

questions.question: For a payments bank account opened through Aadhaar OTP-based e-KYC in a non-face-to-face manner, what is the cap on the customer’s combined balance across deposit accounts, and what must the bank do if that cap is breached?
questions.answer: The combined balance across all of the customer’s deposit accounts must not exceed Rupees One Lakh. If it exceeds that limit, the bank must cease operating the account until it completes the CDD specified in sub-paragraph (5).
questions.evidence: The aggregate balance of all the deposit accounts of the customer shall not exceed Rupees One Lakh. In case the balance exceeds the threshold, the bank shall cease the account’s operation, until it completes the CDD as mentioned at (5) below.

questions.question: For a payments bank account opened using Aadhaar OTP e-KYC, where must the bank send OTPs and transaction alerts, and what must it have in place to handle requests to change the customer’s mobile number?
questions.answer: The bank must send OTPs and transaction alerts only to the mobile number registered with the customer’s Aadhaar. It must also have a Board-approved policy setting out a robust due-diligence process for mobile-number change requests.
questions.evidence: As a risk-mitigating measure for such accounts, the bank shall ensure that it sends transaction alerts, OTP, etc., only to the mobile number of the customer registered with Aadhaar. The bank shall have a Board-approved policy delineating a robust process of due diligence for dealing with requests for change of mobile number in such accounts.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a payments bank send transaction alerts to the Aadhaar-registered mobile number for an account opened through OTP e-KYC?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires transaction alerts to be sent only to the Aadhaar-registered mobile number but does not prescribe any frequency or minimum number of alerts.

questions.question: What must a Regional Rural Bank do to mitigate and manage identified risks under a risk-based approach?
questions.answer: It must apply a risk-based approach and have policies, controls and procedures for managing those risks approved by its Board.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard.

questions.question: When designing and overseeing its customer due diligence programme, what should a Regional Rural Bank consider, and what must it do if its controls need strengthening?
questions.answer: The programme should reflect identified money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks and the size of the bank’s business. The bank must monitor control implementation and enhance the controls when necessary.
questions.evidence: The bank shall implement a CDD programme, having regard to the ML / TF risks identified and the size of business. Further, the bank shall monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them if necessary.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a Regional Rural Bank review the effectiveness of its customer due diligence controls?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring and enhancement of controls but does not specify any review frequency, deadline, or other timing requirement.

questions.question: For an urban co-operative bank using a commercial bank’s at-par cheque facility for KYC-compliant account holders, at what transaction value must payments be strictly debited to the customer’s account?
questions.answer: All transactions of ₹50,000 or more must be strictly by debit to the customers’ accounts.
questions.evidence: (b) for their account-holders who are KYC complaint, provided that all transactions of ₹50,000 or more are strictly by debit to the customers’ accounts,

questions.question: For an urban co-operative bank issuing cheques under a commercial bank’s at-par cheque facility, how must those cheques be crossed regardless of their amount?
questions.answer: The cheques must be crossed ‘account payee’, irrespective of the amount involved.
questions.evidence: ensure that ‘At par’ cheques issued are crossed ‘account payee’ irrespective of the amount involved.

unanswerable.question: For an urban co-operative bank using a commercial bank’s at-par cheque facility, how frequently must the arrangement be reviewed to assess credit and reputational risk?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring and review of the arrangement but does not specify any review frequency, interval, or deadline.

questions.question: What must an Urban Co-operative Bank do at the governance level to manage risks relevant to its customer due diligence obligations?
questions.answer: It must apply a Risk Based Approach and have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures for mitigating and managing those risks.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard.

questions.question: How must an Urban Co-operative Bank tailor and oversee its customer due diligence programme in light of money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks?
questions.answer: It must implement a CDD programme that considers the identified ML/TF risks and the size of its business. It must also monitor the controls and strengthen them when necessary.
questions.evidence: The bank shall implement a CDD programme, having regard to the ML / TF risks identified and the size of business. Further, the bank shall monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them if necessary.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an Urban Co-operative Bank review its CDD controls to confirm that they remain effective?
unanswerable.why: The text requires monitoring controls and enhancing them if necessary, but it specifies no review frequency or deadline.

questions.question: For a rural co-operative bank using a commercial bank’s at-par cheque facility, what uses are permitted and what conditions apply to customer transactions?
questions.answer: The facility may be used for the bank’s own purposes, for KYC-compliant account holders when every transaction of ₹50,000 or more is debited directly to the customer’s account, and for walk-in customers paying cash below ₹50,000 per individual.
questions.evidence:
ensure that the ‘at par’ cheque facility is utilised only:
(a) for their own use,
(b) for their account-holders who are KYC complaint, provided that all transactions of ₹50,000 or more are strictly by debit to the customers’ accounts,
(c) for walk-in customers against cash for less than ₹50,000 per individual.

questions.question: Must a rural co-operative bank cross every at-par cheque it issues as ‘account payee’, even when the amount is below ₹50,000?
questions.answer: Yes. Every at-par cheque issued by a rural co-operative bank must be crossed ‘account payee’, irrespective of the amount involved.
questions.evidence: ensure that ‘At par’ cheques issued are crossed ‘account payee’ irrespective of the amount involved.

unanswerable.question: Is there any daily or monthly cap on the total value of at-par cheques that a rural co-operative bank may issue under a commercial bank’s facility?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph specifies permitted uses and a ₹50,000 per-transaction condition, but it states no aggregate daily or monthly limit on the value of at-par cheques issued.

questions.question: What must a rural co-operative bank do to manage risks through its policies, controls and procedures?
questions.answer: It must apply a risk-based approach to mitigating and managing identified risks and obtain Board approval for the related policies, controls and procedures.
questions.evidence: The bank shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard.

questions.question: How should a rural co-operative bank design and oversee its customer due diligence programme in light of money laundering and terrorist financing risks?
questions.answer: The programme should reflect the ML/TF risks identified and the size of the bank’s business. The bank should also monitor the effectiveness of its controls and strengthen them when necessary.
questions.evidence: The bank shall implement a CDD programme, having regard to the ML / TF risks identified and the size of business. Further, the bank shall monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them if necessary.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must a rural co-operative bank review its customer due diligence controls with the Board?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires monitoring the controls and enhancing them if necessary, but it does not specify any review frequency, interval or deadline.

questions.question: For a new account-based customer relationship, within what deadline must an All India Financial Institution (AIFI) upload the customer’s KYC records to the Central KYC Records Registry (CKYCR)?
questions.answer: The AIFI must upload the customer’s KYC records to CKYCR within 10 days after the account-based relationship commences.
questions.evidence: In terms of provision of Rule 9(1A) of the PML Rules, the AIFI shall capture customer’s KYC records and upload onto CKYCR within 10 days of commencement of an account-based relationship with the customer.

questions.question: After an All India Financial Institution obtains additional or updated information about a customer, how quickly must it furnish that information to CKYCR?
questions.answer: It must furnish the updated information within seven days, or within such period as may be notified by the Central Government.
questions.evidence: Also, whenever the AIFI obtains additional or updated information from any customer as per clause (10) below in this paragraph or Rule 9 (1C) of the PML Rules, the AIFI shall within seven days or within such period as may be notified by the Central Government, furnish the updated information to CKYCR

unanswerable.question: For a legal-entity account opened before April 1, 2021, what is the maximum number of days an All India Financial Institution may take to upload the customer’s KYC record to CKYCR if no updated customer information is received?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires legacy legal-entity KYC records to be uploaded or updated at the time of periodic updation, or earlier when updated information is obtained, but it does not state a separate maximum number of days for that upload.

questions.question: As a small finance bank, who has to approve our KYC policy, and can we delegate that approval to a committee?
questions.answer: The Board of Directors must approve the KYC policy. Approval may be given by a committee to which the Board has delegated that power.
questions.evidence: The Board of Directors of the AIFI, or any committee to which the power has been delegated shall duly approve the KYC policy.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what do we need in place when a customer asks to change the mobile number registered to an account opened without face-to-face interaction?
questions.answer: We need Board-approved policies that describe a robust due diligence process for handling those mobile-number change requests.
questions.evidence: Furthermore, the AIFI shall have the policies approved by the Board detailing a robust due diligence process for managing requests to change the registered Mobile Number for Accounts opened in non-face-to-face mode.

unanswerable.question: As a small finance bank, within how many working days must we complete the due diligence review of a mobile-number change request for an account opened without face-to-face interaction?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires a robust due diligence process but does not specify any deadline for completing the review.

questions.question: At a small finance bank, which registration and tax-identification documents must we obtain before opening an account for a trust?
questions.answer: We must obtain certified copies, or equivalent e-documents, of the trust’s registration certificate, trust deed, and PAN or Form No.60.
questions.evidence:
For opening an account of a trust, certified copies of each of the following documents or the equivalent e-documents thereof shall be obtained:
(1) Registration certificate
(2) Trust deed
(3) PAN or Form No.60 of the trust

questions.question: At an NBFC, whose details and which office address must we collect when opening a trust account?
questions.answer: We must collect the names of the beneficiaries, trustees, settlor, protector (if any), and authors of the trust, along with the trust’s registered office address.
questions.evidence:
(5) the names of the beneficiaries, trustees, settlor, protector, if any and authors of the trust
(6) the address of the registered office of the trust

unanswerable.question: At a small finance bank, how long must we retain the trust’s KYC documents after closing the account?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists documents required to open a trust account but does not specify any post-closure retention period for those documents.

questions.question: At what transaction amount should a small finance bank investigate whether a customer is deliberately splitting transactions to stay under the reporting or identification limit?
questions.answer: The bank should investigate at ₹50,000. If it has reason to believe that a customer, whether account-based or walk-in, is intentionally structuring transactions into a series below ₹50,000, it must undertake customer identification.
questions.evidence: When the AIFI has reason to believe that a customer (account-based or walk-in) is intentionally structuring a transaction into a series of transactions below the threshold of ₹50,000.

questions.question: Can a small finance bank ask an existing customer to refer a prospective new customer when opening an account?
questions.answer: No. The bank must ensure that it does not seek introductions while opening accounts.
questions.evidence: The AIFI shall ensure it does not seek introductions while opening accounts.

unanswerable.question: How long does a small finance bank have to complete customer identification after an account-based relationship with a customer begins?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires identification upon commencement of an account-based relationship but does not state any deadline or time period within which the identification must be completed.

questions.question: Do the RBI’s 2025 KYC/AML Directions apply to an All India Financial Institution’s branches and majority-owned subsidiaries located abroad?
questions.answer: Yes. They apply to an AIFI’s overseas branches and majority-owned subsidiaries, except to the extent that their implementation would conflict with local law in the host country.
questions.evidence: These directions shall also apply to those branches and majority-owned subsidiaries of the AIFI which are located abroad, to the extent they are not contradictory to the local laws in the host country

questions.question: When RBI and host-country KYC/AML standards differ for an All India Financial Institution’s overseas branch or majority-owned subsidiary, which standards must the institution follow?
questions.answer: The institution must follow the more stringent of the RBI-prescribed KYC/AML standards and the host-country regulator’s standards.
questions.evidence: in case there is a variance in KYC / AML standards prescribed by the RBI and the host country regulators, branches / subsidiaries of the AIFI shall adopt the more stringent regulation of the two.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an All India Financial Institution notify the RBI when host-country law prohibits implementation of the RBI’s KYC/AML requirements?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the AIFI to bring the prohibition to the RBI’s notice but does not specify a notification deadline or any number of days.

questions.question: As an NBFC, if we are late in reporting a transaction to the FIU-IND, how many violations do we incur because of the delay?
questions.answer: Each day of delay is treated as a separate violation, so the lateness is counted day by day rather than as one single breach.
questions.evidence: a delay of each day in not reporting a transaction or delay of each day in rectifying a mis-represented transaction beyond the time limit as specified in the Rule shall constitute as a separate violation

questions.question: As an NBFC, may we restrict operations in a customer's account simply because we have filed a suspicious transaction report with the FIU-IND?
questions.answer: No. An NBFC must not place any restriction on operations in the account merely on the basis of the STR filed.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall not put any restriction on operations in the accounts merely on the basis of the STR filed.

unanswerable.question: What is the time limit in days for an NBFC to report a transaction to the Director, FIU-IND, and to correct a mis-reported transaction?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only refers to a time limit 'as specified in the Rule' and states that each day of delay beyond it is a separate violation; it does not state the actual number of days allowed for reporting or rectification.

questions.question: When can an NBFC move a customer's account to a different branch of the same NBFC without carrying out fresh KYC checks?
questions.answer: An NBFC may transfer an account to any other branch or office of the same NBFC relying on the KYC verification already completed, provided the full KYC verification for that account has been done and is not due for periodic updation.
questions.evidence: KYC verification once done by one branch / office of the NBFC shall be valid for transfer of the account to any other branch / office of the same NBFC, provided the NBFC has already completed the full KYC verification for the concerned account and the same is not due for periodic updation.

questions.question: Can an NBFC rely on KYC verification carried out by a different NBFC when it receives a customer from another NBFC's branch?
questions.answer: No. The allowance for carrying over KYC verification is confined to branches or offices of the same NBFC, so verification done by another NBFC is not covered by this provision.
questions.evidence: KYC verification once done by one branch / office of the NBFC shall be valid for transfer of the account to any other branch / office of the same NBFC

unanswerable.question: What customer due diligence measures must an NBFC follow when the account holder is a sole proprietorship firm?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph only carries the heading 'B. CDD Measures for Sole Proprietary firms' and sets out no actual measures, requirements, or conditions for sole proprietorship firms.

questions.question: As an NBFC, what must we do when account monitoring indicates that a customer account is being used as a money mule to launder the proceeds of fraud?
questions.answer: We must perform due diligence and closely monitor the account, take appropriate action, and report the suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.
questions.evidence: The NBFC shall undertake diligence measures and meticulous monitoring to identify accounts which are operated as Money Mules and take appropriate action, including reporting of suspicious transactions to FIU-IND.

questions.question: If an NBFC establishes that an account it opened and operates is being used by a money mule but did not file an STR, what regulatory consequence applies?
questions.answer: The NBFC will be deemed to have not complied with the Directions.
questions.evidence: Further, if it is established that an account opened and operated is that of a Money Mule, but no STR was filed by the concerned NBFC, it shall then be deemed that the NBFC has not complied with these directions.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an NBFC file an STR with FIU-IND after establishing that an account is being operated as a money mule?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires suspicious transactions to be reported to FIU-IND but does not specify a filing deadline.

questions.question: As an Asset Reconstruction Company, how often must we review our money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment, and who decides how often the exercise is carried out?
questions.answer: The Board, or a Board committee to which it has delegated that power, sets the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise; regardless of that, the ARC must review the assessment at least annually.
questions.evidence: Further, the Board or a committee of the Board to which the power has been delegated shall determine the periodicity of the risk assessment exercise, in alignment with the outcome of the risk assessment exercise. However, the ARC shall review it at least annually.

questions.question: What must an Asset Reconstruction Company do with the results of its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment beyond reporting them internally?
questions.answer: Besides presenting the outcome to the Board or a delegated Board committee, the ARC must also make the outcome available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.
questions.evidence: The ARC shall present the outcome of the exercise to the Board or any committee of the Board to which the power has been delegated in this regard. The outcome shall also be made available to competent authorities and self-regulating bodies.

unanswerable.question: What specific risk-rating categories, scoring methodology, or risk matrix must an Asset Reconstruction Company use when conducting its money laundering and terrorist financing risk assessment?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires the ARC to assess and document its ML/TF risk and to align the assessment periodicity with the outcome, but it does not prescribe any rating scale, scoring method, risk categories, or matrix.

questions.question: As an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC), what do we need in place to manage the money-laundering and terrorist-financing risks we identify ourselves?
questions.answer: An ARC must apply a risk-based approach to mitigating and managing identified risks and have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures for this purpose. It must also implement a customer due diligence (CDD) programme that takes account of the ML/TF risks identified and the size of its business.
questions.evidence: The ARC shall apply a Risk Based Approach (RBA) for mitigation and management of the risks (identified on its own or through national risk assessment) and shall have Board-approved policies, controls and procedures in this regard. The ARC shall implement a CDD programme, having regard to the ML / TF risks identified and the size of business.

questions.question: Once our CDD programme is running, what ongoing oversight must an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC) perform over its controls?
questions.answer: The ARC must monitor whether its controls are actually being implemented and enhance them where necessary.
questions.evidence: Further, the ARC shall monitor the implementation of the controls and enhance them if necessary.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC) review its Board-approved KYC policies and CDD programme to confirm they remain adequate?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires Board-approved policies, controls and procedures, a CDD programme, and monitoring and enhancement of controls, but it does not state any review frequency, deadline, or time period for such review.

questions.question: What must an Asset Reconstruction Company do if a non-profit organisation customer is not registered on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog?
questions.answer: The ARC must register the non-profit organisation customer's details on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog.
questions.evidence: The ARC shall ensure that in case of customers who are non-profit organisations, the details of such customers are registered on the DARPAN Portal of NITI Aayog. If they are not registered, the ARC shall register the details on the DARPAN Portal.

questions.question: How long must an Asset Reconstruction Company retain DARPAN registration records for a non-profit organisation customer after the business relationship ends or the account is closed?
questions.answer: The ARC must retain the registration records for five years after the business relationship ends or the account is closed, whichever is later.
questions.evidence: The ARC shall also maintain such registration records for a period of five years after the business relationship between the customer and the ARC has ended or the account has been closed, whichever is later.

unanswerable.question: Within how many days must an Asset Reconstruction Company register a non-profit organisation customer on the DARPAN Portal after establishing the business relationship?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires registration but does not specify a deadline or number of days for completing it.

questions.question: As an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC), can we acquire a financial asset or account if the transferor bank or financial institution has not yet completed the customer’s KYC?
questions.answer: No. An ARC must not acquire a financial asset or account while KYC remains pending at the transferor bank or financial institution.
questions.evidence: Also, ARC shall ensure not to acquire financial assets / accounts where KYC (i.e. customer identification and verification of customer’s identity) is pending at the level of transferor bank / financial institution.

questions.question: As an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC), what customer due diligence must we perform for the holders when opening a joint account?
questions.answer: We must follow the CDD procedure for every joint account holder when opening the joint account.
questions.evidence: (7) follow the CDD Procedure for all the joint account holders, while opening a joint account.

unanswerable.question: How frequently must an Asset Reconstruction Company update the KYC information it collects from customers?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires mandatory KYC information to be sought during periodic updation, but it does not state any interval or frequency for that updation.

questions.question: As a compliance officer at an Asset Reconstruction Company (ARC), what must we do with a customer’s PAN when undertaking transactions?
questions.answer: We must obtain and verify the customer’s PAN or equivalent e-document in accordance with Income Tax Rule 114B applicable to ARCs, as amended from time to time.
questions.evidence: PAN or equivalent e-document thereof of customers shall be obtained and verified while undertaking transactions as per the provisions of Income Tax Rule 114B applicable to ARCs, as amended from time to time.

questions.question: At an Asset Reconstruction Company, what document must we obtain from a customer who does not have a PAN or equivalent e-document?
questions.answer: We must obtain Form 60 from that customer.
questions.evidence: Form 60 shall be obtained from persons who do not have PAN or equivalent e-document thereof.

unanswerable.question: What is the deadline for an Asset Reconstruction Company to verify a customer’s PAN after obtaining it?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph requires ARCs to obtain and verify PAN or an equivalent e-document while undertaking transactions, but it does not specify any verification deadline or number of days.

questions.question: As an NBFC subject to the RBI's credit information reporting requirements, is our industry represented on the Technical Working Group?
questions.answer: Yes. Representatives from Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs) are among the members of the Technical Working Group.
questions.evidence: The TWG shall comprise of representatives from Public Sector Banks, Private Sector Banks, Foreign Banks, Primary (Urban) Cooperative Banks (UCBs), Regional Rural Banks (RRBs), All India Notified Financial Institutions (AIFIs), Non-Banking Financial Companies (NBFCs), Housing Finance Companies (HFCs), Asset Reconstruction Companies (ARCs) India Banks’ Association (IBA), Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN), Sa-Dhan and CICs.

questions.question: Which industry associations and networks are included in the Technical Working Group's membership?
questions.answer: The Technical Working Group includes the India Banks’ Association (IBA), the Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN), Sa-Dhan and CICs.
questions.evidence: India Banks’ Association (IBA), Micro Finance Institutions Network (MFIN), Sa-Dhan and CICs.

unanswerable.question: How many representatives may an NBFC appoint to the Technical Working Group, and by what date must the nomination be submitted?
unanswerable.why: The paragraph lists NBFCs among the categories whose representatives form the TWG, but it does not state any number of representatives per category, nor any nomination process or deadline.

questions.question: As an NBFC compliance officer, how frequently must the Technical Working Group (TWG) meet?
questions.answer: The TWG must meet at least once in each calendar year.
questions.evidence: Meetings of the TWG shall be held at least once in a calendar year.

questions.question: Who is responsible for convening the Technical Working Group (TWG) in a given calendar year?
questions.answer: The four CICs must act as convenor by rotation each calendar year, in alphabetical order of their names.
questions.evidence: The four CICs shall act as convenor of the TWG by rotation (for each calendar year), in alphabetical order of the name.

unanswerable.question: By what date within the calendar year must the Technical Working Group hold its meeting?
unanswerable.why: The rule states only that the TWG must meet at least once in a calendar year; it does not specify any deadline or date within the year.

questions.question: As an NBFC that is a Credit Information Company covered under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, what is required of us under that Scheme?
questions.answer: Your NBFC must comply with the directions provided under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme (RB-IOS).
questions.evidence: A CI covered under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, (RB-IOS) as amended from time to time, shall comply with the directions provided under the said Scheme.

questions.question: If the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme is amended, which version of its directions must an NBFC that is a Credit Information Company covered under it follow?
questions.answer: It must follow the directions under the Scheme as amended from time to time, that is, the Scheme in its current amended form.
questions.evidence: A CI covered under the Reserve Bank – Integrated Ombudsman Scheme, (RB-IOS) as amended from time to time, shall comply with the directions provided under the said Scheme.
